subject: english-language
title: Post-Telegraphic Mastery
welcome_lead: Function words snap into place, morphology stabilises, complex syntax arrives. The final acquisition stage.
meta_desc: Post-telegraphic stage, morphology and complex syntax in child language acquisition at A-Level.
final_note: You have completed the developmental journey — by five, the child commands the system, give or take a few irregulars.

concepts.def: From around 30 months: function words reappear, morphology and complex syntax develop.
Jean Berko Gleason's 1958 test showed children could pluralise nonsense words (wugs), demonstrating internal rule knowledge.
Children master inflections in a predictable order — Brown's stages I-V.
Applying a regular pattern to an irregular form (goed, mouses), peaking after irregulars are first learned.
Coordination (and) appears first; subordination (because, when) follows.
Roger Brown's MLU-based progression from Stage I (1.75) to Stage V (4.0+), each tied to grammatical milestones.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Berko Gleason (1958) showed children a creature labelled wug, then a second one: Now there are two.. Children supplied wugs — a form they had never heard.

The experiment is decisive evidence that children internalise productive rules, not just store memorised forms.

A child may first say went correctly (memorised), then start saying goed as the regular past-tense rule takes hold, then recover went as the irregular exception is reinstated.

This U-shaped curve is a classic signature of rule-learning.

Coordination (I had cake and Sam had ice cream) appears before subordination. Causal because arrives early; temporal when shortly after; concessive although later.

By age five most children command the major syntactic structures of the adult grammar.

mcqs.q: What is the telegraphic stage of child language development?
options: Chomsky said children should be taught grammar from age two.
Around age 2-3, children produce short utterances containing content words but omitting function words and inflections (e.g. 'mummy gone shop').
It is the stage when children first start using a telephone.
It is the stage where children memorise long stories.

mcqs.q: How does Piaget's theory relate language to cognitive development?
options: Piaget said language drives cognitive development.
Piaget was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.
Chomsky said children should be taught grammar from age two.

Language develops as a consequence of cognitive development — children must first develop concepts (object permanence, conservation) before they can express them linguistically. Cognition leads language.

mcqs.q: What did Chomsky propose about language acquisition?
options: Chomsky said children should be taught grammar from age two.
It is the stage where children memorise long stories.
Children possess an innate Language Acquisition Device — an inborn capacity for grammar — because exposure alone cannot account for how rapidly and uniformly children learn complex syntax.
Chomsky said children learn language entirely by copying adults.
